notes: Nuisance/damages case re: soot and vibration from an electric plant fouling a hotel; measure-of-damages dispute, not about the legal character or regulation of letting rooms.
Civil rights statute case holding a bootblacking stand is not a 'place of public accommodation'; no bearing on lodging/letting rooms despite listing inns/hotels in the statute's enumeration.
Contract/assignment and patent-damages dispute over printing presses and a restraint-of-trade covenant; 'lease' language refers to leasing presses to purchasers, unrelated to dwelling occupancy.

Home-rule constitutional challenge to the office of state superintendent of elections; mentions power to inspect hotels/lodging-houses and require lodger registers as an investigative tool only, not a case about the legal character of letting rooms.

Cattle-trespass liability case discussing fencing statutes and 'incident of ownership' of land; unrelated to letting dwellings/rooms.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Plaintiffs bought a lease of premises operated as a rooming house, along with the furniture, but a provision of the underlying lease restricted use of the premises 'solely as a private dwelling,' preventing them from taking roomers; the court held a temporary injunction against enforcement of the purchase-money notes and chattel mortgage was improperly granted because plaintiffs neither tendered back the property nor sought rescission, and had an adequate remedy at law.

quotes.text: The plaintiffs bought of the defendants a lease of premises containing a rooming house and the business therein conducted, and the furniture therein, and claim that it was represented that the house could be used for the purpose of a rooming house and that the furniture therein was the defendant-seller’s property.

They allege that the furniture was not defendants’ property and thereafter was removed, and that they cannot use the house for roomers by reason of a provision of the lease that it may be used solely as a private dwelling.

notes: Case recites (but does not itself adjudicate the merits of) a lease clause confining the premises to 'private dwelling' use and excluding rooming-house operation, an adverse-leaning fact pattern; the court's actual holding is on equity procedure (rescission/tender), so characterization is left null since the court did not itself classify the arrangement.
